messages:
Maya (Support): FYI customer pinged — production p95/p99 for text-generation jumped ~3x starting 11:02 UTC. They see long queueing delays and 503s. attaching brief logs.

Ajay (Eng Runtime): can you paste the request ids / example timestamps? which model / route?

Maya (Support): route: /v1/generate (model: redwood-medium-1). Sample request ids: req_8a7c, req_8a8f. Customer claims spikes coincide with a batch job at 11:00 UTC that increases concurrency.

Maya (Support): log snippet:
```
2026-03-14T11:02:03Z req_8a7c queue_wait=420ms worker_acquire=:: timed_out?=false error=none
2026-03-14T11:02:03Z req_8a8f queue_wait=1800ms worker_acquire=500ms served=120ms status=200
2026-03-14T11:02:05Z req_8a90 queue_wait=3200ms admitted=false failure=backpressure_limit_reached status=503
```

Taylor (SRE): that looks like admission control tripping + overloaded workers. any surge protection events in the past hour?

deploy-bot: @channel rolling deploy of autoscaler config to staging succeeded at 10:58 UTC.

Ajay (Eng Runtime): can we confirm worker pool saturation metrics? @Taylor can you check GPUs occupied / queue depth around 11:00?

Taylor (SRE): checking Prometheus now. p99 queue depth across cluster spiked to 4200 reqs at 11:01. GPU utilization at that time: 98%. CPU/IO fine. There were several long-running requests with large seq lengths.

Olivia (Customer Success): customer is on Dedicated. They want immediate mitigation — asked for a short-term workaround before we root-cause.

Ajay (Eng Runtime): short-term options: 1) increase per-customer concurrency for that Dedicated pool (if headroom exists), 2) enable degraded serving path (smaller model/quantized variant) for canary, 3) temporary tightening of admission control to favor low-latency routes (reject large seqs). Which is quickest?

Taylor (SRE): option 3 is fastest (config flip), but could increase 503s for long-seq jobs. option 2 requires rolling model variant but can be fast if model already cached. option 1 requires capacity allocation which could be delayed.

Maya (Support): customer prefers option 2 (fallback to redwood-medium-1-quant) for latency-sensitive endpoints. They said quality tradeoff ok for 1 hour.

Ajay (Eng Runtime): ok. I can push a routing-policy change to route model fallback for that customer id. drafting command.

Ajay (Eng Runtime): apply routing policy:
```
PATCH /api/v1/policies/route-customer-12345
{
  "match": {"customer_id": "cust-12345", "route": "/v1/generate"},
  "action": {"fallback_model": "redwood-medium-1-quant", "priority": 5, "duration": "60m"}
}
```

Taylor (SRE): before applying, note that quantized variant has slightly different kernel memory patterns — should check per-GPU memory footprint so we don't spike OOMs.

Ajay (Eng Runtime): good call. checking cache status: quant variant cached on 3/5 GPUs in the pool. memory usage: ~8GB less per replica. That should help throughput.

deploy-bot: @Ajay policy patch queued; run `deploy apply route-customer-12345` to execute.

Ajay (Eng Runtime): running now.

deploy-bot: policy route-customer-12345 applied at 11:12 UTC.

Maya (Support): customer reports noticeable improvement at 11:15 — p95 back to baseline, p99 improved but still slightly elevated. They still see occasional 503s for large-batch jobs.

Taylor (SRE): observing queue depth falling from 4200 -> 300 over 10 minutes. GPU util down to 85%. Good. We should follow up with a permanent fix.

Olivia (Customer Success): customer asked for postmortem and next steps to avoid repeat. I'll coordinate.

Ajay (Eng Runtime): root cause hypothesis: unbounded background batch job from customer that launches many long seq requests simultaneously. Combined with insufficient admission thresholds (admit based on slot rather than seq length) led to worker pileup and KV cache thrashing.

Taylor (SRE): agreed. data: high variance in sequence lengths during spike. KV cache miss rate jumped. We also saw per-request memory growth for some tensor allocations.

Maya (Support): repro steps for internal follow-up: customer supplied a load generator: 1000 clients each sending 1 request every 2s with seq_len ~2048 for 5 minutes. They ran it accidentally during business hours.

Ajay (Eng Runtime): proposed longer-term mitigations: - admission control should consider estimated token cost (seq_len * tokens) not just concurrent connections; - implement soft-priority buckets (latency-sensitive vs batch) with time-slicing; - auto-fallback for heavy requests to cheaper variants or queued offline processing; - proactive per-customer burst protection with notifications.

Taylor (SRE): I'll open an incident follow-up ticket and add metrics we missed (per-customer seq_len histograms, KV cache miss alarms, estimated token backlog)

Maya (Support): customer asked for an SLA credit estimate. Finance please advise? cc @Olivia

Olivia (Customer Success): I'll take lead on SLA discussion and coordinate with finance.

Ajay (Eng Runtime): action items: Ajay -> implement token-cost admission prototype (PR by EOD), Taylor -> create follow-up incident ticket + alerts, Maya -> send customer summary + temporary mitigation timeline, Olivia -> SLA coordination.

Maya (Support): sending summary now to customer: includes repro, mitigation applied (fallback to quant variant), ETA for permanent changes.

Olivia (Customer Success): customer acknowledged and said they'd avoid running large internal batch during peak for now. :relieved:

Taylor (SRE): closing loop: marking monitoring as green. Will keep on pager for next 24h.

Ajay (Eng Runtime): thanks everyone. we'll follow up with design doc for token-aware admission and priority buckets.

Maya (Support): thanks all :thumbsup:
